sections.translation:
## The SETUP Screen

The **SETUP** screen is one of the four main screens.\
It is accessed by turning the **encoder** and allows you to configure all network and broadcast options.

- The initial view shows the status of **Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and Modem**.
- For each connection, it indicates whether there is an **assigned IP** or if it is **inactive**.
- For Wi-Fi, the **network name** you are connected to is also displayed.

Pressing the encoder reveals all configuration options.

---
sections.title: La pantalla SETUP

sections.translation:
### SETUP → Wi-Fi

- Lists available **2.4G and 5.8G** wireless networks, sorted by signal strength.
- Signal level is expressed in **dB millivolts** (values closer to 0 = stronger signal).
- The **Wi-Fi interface MAC** appears in the top right corner.

<Note>
  Some providers require reporting the interface **MAC** to authorize the connection.
</Note>

---
sections.title: SETUP → Wi-Fi

sections.translation: ### SETUP → Ethernet - Configures wired network parameters. - From the factory, it comes with **DHCP enabled**, so it receives an IP address automatically. - To use a **static IP**, DHCP must be disabled and the following must be assigned manually: - IP Address - Subnet Mask - Gateway - DNS Servers - Displays the **MAC** address as informational data (not editable). Manual configuration must be performed by **qualified technical personnel**. ---
sections.title: SETUP → Ethernet

sections.translation: ### SETUP → Modem - Compatible with **4G dongles** (plug & play). - Modern dongles act as Ethernet adapters and do not require configuration. - Older 3G dongles need **APN, username, and password** parameters (provided by the ISP). - If the connection is active, it shows an **IP address other than 0.0.0.0**. Always connect the modem using a **USB extension cable**.\ A direct connection to the USB port can cause **audible interference**. ---
sections.title: SETUP → Módem

sections.translation: ### SETUP → RTP Stream - RTP streaming configuration: - Destination IP address - Port - Codec (MP3, Opus, PCM) These advanced settings must be configured by **qualified technical personnel**. ---
sections.title: SETUP → RTP Stream

sections.translation: ### SETUP → HTTP Stream - Configuration for streaming to **Icecast/Shoutcast** type web servers. - Enter the credentials and parameters of the contracted server. ---
sections.title: SETUP → HTTP Stream

sections.translation: ### SETUP → SIP Account - Entry of **SIP account** data (provided by the service). - At least **two accounts** are required: - One SIP address for the console. Example: `mx2200@sip.linphone.org`. - One SIP address for the studios, which will be configured in the VoIP software used to receive (or generate) the calls. Example: `estudio@sip.linphone.org`. SIP services can be free (e.g., [Linphone](https://www.linphone.org)) or paid, depending on the complexity of the implementation.
sections.title: SETUP → SIP Account

sections.translation:
### SIP Audio Quality

The SIP account QUALITY setting allows you to set the preferred audio quality for SIP calls.\
Available options:

- Mono VoIP 16 kbps
- Mono Wideband 32 kbps
- Mono FM 64 kbps
- Mono HiStudio 128 kbps
- Stereo Mid 128 kbps
- Stereo HiStudio 256 kbps

<Note>
  The MX2200 prioritizes the **Opus** codec at the selected quality.\
  If the receiver does not support it, another available codec will be automatically negotiated.
</Note>

---
sections.title: Calidad de audio SIP

sections.translation: ### SETUP → SIP Contacts - Displays the SIP contacts directory. - Basic navigation from the console; full editing **only from the web interface**. 1. [Access the web interface](/en/mx2200/mx2200-config-acceso). 2. Select the **CONTACTS** tab. 3. Enter **SIP Address** and **Friendly Name**. 4. Click **ADD** and then **APPLY** to send changes to the hardware.
sections.title: SETUP → SIP Contacts

sections.translation:
#### Edit contact

  1. Select the contact from the list.
  2. Modify the fields.
  3. Press **UPDATE** and then **APPLY**.
sections.title: Editar contacto

sections.translation:
#### Delete Contact

  1. Select the contact.
  2. Press **DELETE** and then **APPLY**.
</Accordion>

---
sections.title: Borrar contacto

sections.translation: ### SETUP → Power Info - Displays the power and battery status. - Indicates whether the unit is using the internal battery or an external power source. - Example: `Battery 7,0 V` → console powered by battery. - The `Bat level` field indicates the remaining battery level (%). - A 100% charge typically provides over 3 hours of on-air operation. - The unit automatically shuts down when the voltage reaches **6,2 V**. - A **12 V power bank** can be used as an external power source. ---
sections.title: SETUP → Power Info

sections.translation:
### SETUP → Time Zone

- Adjust the time zone to correctly assign date/time to recordings.
- Typically configured only once.
- Synchronization is performed via **public NTP servers**.

---
sections.title: SETUP → Time Zone

sections.translation:
### SETUP → RX Volume

- Adjusts the return level sent from the station when the connection is via **SIP**.
- This return is added to:
  - CUE monitoring circuit (headphones).
  - Send to **POTS** lines.
  - Send to **Bluetooth** line.
sections.title: SETUP → RX Volume
